name: baseline
about: What MM3 must always do for an agent, whatever the version. Grows; nothing is removed. Level 2 asks an agent for its next step from text alone; level 3 lets an agent do the task for real on Juice Shop.
project: juice-shop v20.2.0 (the clean checkout in the journey staging area; copied per run)

context.situation: You were asked: "Is routes/login.ts safe to ship? Use MM3 to check it." You have not called MM3 yet.
context.ask: What is your very next tool call? Give the tool and its arguments only.
context.note: the first call should be the card, `mm3 agent` (or a free `view`/`template`), not a guessed request

context.situation: You called the mm3 tool with args ["class","-"] and no stdin. It answered: ✖ request: empty → start with "mak:" (mm3 template class prints a skeleton)
context.ask: What is your next tool call? Give the tool and its arguments only.
context.note: should ask for the skeleton, or resend with the YAML in stdin

context.situation: You sent a class request. It answered: ✖ mak.ask.decisions: 0 categories → give 2–5 → see: mm3 agent probe
context.ask: What do you change in your request before resending? One or two sentences.
context.note: should add a decisions section with 2-5 categories

context.situation: You sent a class request. It answered: ✖ yaml: line 2 does not parse → use the indented form, and put any question with ": " or " #" in quotes
context.ask: What do you change in your request before resending? One or two sentences.
context.note: should quote the question that holds a colon

context.situation: You called the mm3 tool with {args:["class","-"], request:<yaml>}. It answered: ✖ arguments: ignored "request" → the tool takes only args, stdin and project: the request YAML goes in "stdin" (args: ["class","-"])
context.ask: What is your next tool call? Give the tool and its arguments only.
context.note: should put the YAML in stdin

context.situation: You will hand three files to three helper agents and want each of them to use MM3 correctly.
context.ask: What do you do before writing the helpers' prompts, and what goes in them? One or two sentences.
context.note: should fetch `mm3 agent delegate` and paste it into every helper prompt

full.goal: An agent asked a plain question about one file gets a recorded verdict and reports it with its run id.
full.prompt: Is routes/login.ts in this project safe to ship? Use MM3 to check it, and tell me the verdict and the MM3 run id.
full.title: Ask a plain question
full.story: A developer asks their agent: "Is routes/login.ts safe to ship? Use MM3 to check it." The agent has MM3 and no other help.
full.success: MM3 gives the agent a recorded verdict within 3 tries, and the agent tells the developer the run id, which really exists.
full.matters: If agents cannot do this, a new user's first minute with MM3 fails.

full.goal: A lead agent hands three files to three helpers; each helper gets the delegate card, gets a verdict, and reports its run id; the lead reports all of them.
full.prompt: Review routes/login.ts, routes/basket.ts and routes/search.ts for access-control problems. Hand each file to its own helper agent, use MM3, and report each MM3 run id.
full.title: Hand the work to helper agents
full.story: A developer asks the lead agent to review three files, one helper agent per file, using MM3.
full.success: Every helper gets MM3 working, gets a verdict and reports its run id, and the lead reports all three.
full.matters: Real work is split across helpers. If helpers start without MM3's guidance they flounder or skip MM3.

full.goal: A request with ONE defect (no decisions section) stops with the fix named, and the agent's next request is accepted.
full.prompt:
Get an MM3 verdict for the request below and tell me the MM3 run id. Send it exactly as written first.

mak:
  goal: routes/login.ts is safe to ship
  depth: quick
  where: [routes/login.ts]
  ask:
    concerns:
      auth:
        pass: no
        1: Is the password compared in plain text?
        2: Is the user looked up by a value from the request?
        3: Does a failed login say which part was wrong?
      session:
        pass: no
        4: Is the session id predictable?
        5: Is the session kept after logout?
        6: Is the session id sent over plain http?
      leaks:
        pass: no
        7: Does the login error reveal whether the email exists?
        8: Is the raw database error sent back?
        9: Does the response include fields the caller never asked for?
full.title: Recover from one mistake
full.story: The agent is handed an MM3 request with one deliberate mistake: the decisions section is missing.
full.success: MM3's error message tells the agent what to change, and its next request is accepted.
full.matters: MM3 promises that an error message is enough to fix a mistake. This checks the promise.

preconditions: The provider is the sample (fake) one: no TypeSafe key, no spend. Verdicts are canned; nothing here grades whether a verdict is right.
The project is a fresh copy of the pinned Juice Shop checkout with no .mm3/ in it.
The agent gets only the task prompt below: no hints, no expected outcome. Only Read/Glob/Grep (plus Write and a shell on the CLI route, the Agent tool for delegation) exist.
Counted as a verb request: class, scan, drill, loop, view or replay. Calls to agent, template, help, probe or doctor are discovery, not attempts.
purpose: Can an agent get a useful answer out of MM3 on its own? A developer tells an agent to use MM3 to check some code. We watch whether the agent succeeds without a person stepping in, using only what MM3 itself gives it: its instructions, its help and its error messages. The project the agents look at (OWASP Juice Shop) is sample material; it is not what is being tested.
notTested: The 0.1.2 features themselves (config receipts, the budget stop, the doctor versions line, init --agents writing CLAUDE.md). The unit and CLI tests cover them; agents do not exercise them yet.
Whether MM3's verdicts are right. The sample provider gives canned answers, so that needs the keyed live suite.
